policy: Separate derived series only; no raw database changes, return clipping or inferred trades. Constants normalize units within a reviewed interval. Do not extrapolate these rules after 2015.

repairs.reason: One new share for ten old shares; first split-adjusted trading session May 28. The supplied adjusted series retains the raw price jump.
One-for-ten reverse split; first split-adjusted trading session October 11. Apply cumulatively with the separate 2010 split.
One-for-fifteen reverse split after the October 19 close; first adjusted session October 20. This corrects a unit discontinuity, not a positive economic return.

The vendor adjusted series switches to 16 times the historical price scale on the NYSE transfer date. Divide this interval by 16, supported by nine exact quarter-end closing-price anchors through 2015 and the issuer's contemporary price ranges. The upstream cause of the 16x scale is not established; this is not described as a 2013 stock split.

anchor_note: The pre-boundary October 2 anchor is from Lannett's October 2013 prospectus. The nine subsequent quarter-end anchors are from a SEC-filed structured-note price history. They validate historical levels, not a predictive feature available earlier. No post-2015 price is used. Between anchors the constant vendor regime is an explicit normalization model, not independent verification of every daily quote.
